title: Signal gardener runbook and dashboard planting plan
content:
Purpose and framing:

This is a lightweight, pragmatic runbook for growing and maintaining a compact, cost-aware observability surface for inference services. Think of signals as plants: some need daily water (high-cardinality live signals), others are perennial (SLIs). The goal of this doc is to: create a repeatable onboarding checklist for new signals, define a small set of metric contracts and tracing anchors, and propose a dashboard "planting plan" (where widgets live and how they age out).

High-level goals (why):
- Maintain operator productivity: short investigation pathways for these specific failure modes: latency spikes, prefix cold-cache events, KV eviction storms, and tenant-induced noise.
- Keep telemetry costs predictable: deliberate signal-budget per service + per-experiment.
- Improve rollouts: instrumented canaries with probe coverage and trace anchors so rollbacks are faster and less noisy.

Signal budgeting model (new):
- Budget concept: each service gets a monthly signal credit measured in "probe-seconds". Heavy traces and full session replays cost more credits; lightweight counters cost almost none.
- Default budget (in pilot): 100k probe-seconds/month for small services, 500k for medium, 2M for large. Teams can petition for more with a migration plan (reduce cardinality, add sampling).
- Enforcement: dashboards show remaining budget; alerts when 75%/90%/100% hit. Owner must sign remediation plan at 100%.

Onboarding checklist for a new signal (quick steps):
1) Describe the hypothesis the signal will test (one sentence).
2) Decide SLI vs telemetry vs debug artifact.
3) Choose cardinality tier: low (global), medium (per-model), high (per-tenant).
4) Assign owner and expected retention (7d/30d/90d).
5) Determine cost impact (probe-seconds estimate) and fit within monthly budget.
6) Add trace anchor(s) and span tag conventions.
7) Add alert threshold and runbook link.
8) Create dashboard widget and mark lifecycle policy (auto-deprecate date).

Metric contract templates (examples):
- inference.latency.p99
  description: end-to-end generation latency 99th percentile (token stream finish).
  type: gauge derived from request timer
  units: milliseconds
  owner: eng-serving-runtime
  sli: yes (customer-perceived latency)

- kvcache.evicts.count
  description: number of KV cache evictions per host per minute
  type: counter
  units: events/minute
  owner: eng-serving-runtime/cache
  sli: no (operational signal)

- tenant.kv.warmth_index
  description: approximate fraction of requests hitting warm cache for a tenant
  type: ratio
  units: percent
  owner: eng-sre
  sli: maybe (used for debugging cold-cache regressions)

Tracing conventions (compact and new rules):
- Root span: request.inference.{model_name} (attach model_name tag)
- Important child spans: kvcache.lookup, kvcache.populate, batch.assemble, executor.kernel.run, response.stream
- Trace anchors: every trace must include these tags when available: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), model_version, route_id, seq_len
- Sampling policy: sample 1/1000 for normal traffic; always sample on error >= 5xx; sample 1/50 for canary routes and for traces with kvcache.populate=true
- Trace size guidelines: keep per-trace span count under 200 where possible. Large traces should be truncated and flagged with span.truncated=true

Dashboard planting plan (widget conventions and lifecycle):
- Widget ink footprint: each dashboard should be < 8 widgets for oncall view, with 1 golden SLI panel and 2–3 triage starter panels (top error classes, p99 latency heatmap, tenant worst offenders).
- Placement: top-left = golden SLI(s). top-right = capacity/cost view (tokens/sec, GPU util). middle = triage panels. bottom = long-tail investigative graphs (session rebuild, trace sampling rates).
- Aging policy: tag every panel with metadata: owner, created_at, retention_policy. Panels older than 270 days without updates are flagged for cleanup.

Debug recipes and investigation flow (operator-first):
1) Check golden SLI(s) for the service. If within SLO, stop.
2) Look at p99 latency slices and heatmap (by route/model/tenant).
3) If p99 jump: check kvcache.evicts.count and tenant.kv.warmth_index; correlate with traffic surge.
4) If related to a rollout: open canary trace anchor and check trace sampling ratio and batch.assemble spans for unexpected delays.
5) Use quickcards (query snippets below) to reconstruct session context for the worst 5 traces in last 10 minutes.

Example quick SQL-like snippets (telemetry store assumed):
- top five tenants by p99 increase:
  SELECT tenant_id, p99_latency_delta FROM telemetry WHERE service='inference' AND window='5m' ORDER BY p99_latency_delta DESC LIMIT 5
- traces with kvcache.populate true and long kernel run:
  SELECT trace_id FROM traces WHERE tags.kvcache.populate=true AND spans.kernel_run_ms > 100 ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 20

Dash ownership and runbook integration (ops hygiene):
- Each dashboard must link to a short runbook (1–2 steps) that the oncall can execute: kill canary, reduce traffic, fallback model variant, flush tenant cache.
- Runbook must include the command snippets and Slack escalation channel.

Experiment guidance (short):
- Any A/B experiment or model swap must estimate telemetry cost delta. Default rule: experiments start with 10% traffic and enhanced trace sampling (1/50) for the variant. The product/experiment owner must accept runbook noise budget.

Migration notes (if we adopt budgets):
- Phase 1: pilot with two services for 2 months to calibrate probe-second weights.
- Phase 2: enforce dashboard budget signals (visual, not blocking).
- Phase 3: automated throttling for high-cost tracing in non-prod when budgets exceeded.

Open questions / discussion items:
- How aggressive should span truncation be for multi-model fanout traces? (tradeoff visibility vs cost)
- Should we add a tenant-weight to budget (small tenants free, enterprise tenants pay)?
- Best way to annotate dashboards with budget burn rate in real time?

Action items (next steps):
- [ ] Pilot budget telemetry for inference-stable service (owners: Ravi + Lena) — due 2025-04-01
- [ ] Add onboarding checklist template to Confluence (owner: Maya) — due 2025-03-20
- [ ] Build probe-seconds calculator microservice and UI widget (owner: eng-telemetry) — spike due 2025-03-28

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep widget count small. Avoid large per-tenant panels on the main oncall dash; use followups.
- Consider a second "gardening" cadence: quarterly review of signals to compost (delete/low-retain).
- This doc intentionally mixes metaphor and concrete templates — fine for internal workshop, will be cleaned for a canonical playbook later.

Appendix: mini glossary
- probe-seconds: a synthetic currency that approximates cost of a metric or trace sample over time.
- trace anchor: a span or tag used to quickly locate the relevant trace for a particular investigation (e.g., kvcache.populate=true).
- warmth_index: a heuristic (0..1) describing cache hit probability for a tenant.

If you want, I can convert selected sections into a one-page runbook or a Confluence template (onboarding checklist + metric contract table).
